description: Given two strings word1 and word2, merge them by adding letters in alternating order starting with word1. If one string is longer, append the remaining letters at the end.
intuition: Think of it like shuffling two decks of cards together - take one card from each deck alternately. When one deck runs out, just add the remaining cards from the other deck.
approach: Use two pointers to iterate through both strings simultaneously, appending one character from each. After the loop, append whatever remains from the longer string.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: word1 = "abc", word2 = "pqr"
i=0: push word1[0]="a", push word2[0]="p" -> result=["a","p"]
i=1: push word1[1]="b", push word2[1]="q" -> result=["a","p","b","q"]
i=2: push word1[2]="c", push word2[2]="r" -> result=["a","p","b","q","c","r"]
i=3: both lengths exhausted, loop ends
Return "apbqcr"
explanation:
1. Use a single index i to traverse both strings.
2. At each step, append word1[i] if it exists, then word2[i] if it exists.
3. Continue until both strings are exhausted.
4. Join the result list into a string.
hints: Handle the case where strings have different lengths.
Use a list and join for efficient string building.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: n = word1 length; m = word2 length.
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Each input character is appended once and copied once into the final string.
